jobs.title: Data QA Engineer - Remote
jobs.description: At Zyte, we eat data for breakfast and you can eat your breakfast anywhere and work for Zyte. Founded in 2010, we are a globally distributed team of over 250 Zytans working from over 28 countries who are on a mission to enable our customers to extract the data they need to continue to innovate and grow their businesses. We believe that all businesses deserve a smooth pathway to data. Role Overview Data QA is how we make sure the data we deliver is right before the customer sees it. As a Data QA Engineer, you will check the data our spiders and AI-assisted projects produce against what the customer asked for, find what is wrong and tell the team exactly what you found. Quality assurance is more useful as a question asked at the start than a gate at the end. Is this requirement testable and how would we know if it were wrong? Part of this role is asking that question early, so problems are fixed before they reach the customer. Key Responsibilities Turn customer scraping and data requirements into a clear test approach and own QA from the start on new projects. Combine exploratory manual and visual testing with automated tests where automation pays for itself. Run test cycles on extracted data and report the results clearly. Write up defects with enough detail that a developer can reproduce and fix them without a conversation. Use descriptive statistics, summaries and charts to show how good the data is: completeness, accuracy, consistency and drift. Produce test reports and quality scores that give the team, and the customer where needed, a true picture. Say what was tested, what was not, and what risk that leaves. Work with project managers and clients to clear up unclear or untestable requirements before QA begins. Feed into our test automation framework, with a focus on coverage and performance. Suggest and take ownership of improvements to QA process and tooling, including browser add-ons, spreadsheet add-ons and UI-based test automation tools. Work with QA leadership, project managers and developers, with minimal supervision. 5+ years in a QA Engineer or similar role - testing software or data. Python preferred language - Pandas and Jupyter for data analysis and validation. SQL: basic to intermediate queries, and comfort with at least one relational database and its tools. A solid grasp of web technologies and protocols: HTML, XPath, JSON, HTTP and CSS. Experience writing tests against HTTP/REST APIs. Proactive and detail-oriented QA professional with a strong sense of ownership over project quality. Fast learner adept at rapidly understanding complex project domain requirements and adapting to new technologies. Leveraging AI and LLM tools to optimize test case generation and accelerate data validation processes. Good test case design and test data management. Experience working in an agile team (Scrum or Kanban) alongside developers. An understanding of data quality concepts such as completeness, accuracy, consistency and drift. Strong attention to detail, and the confidence to hold the quality line under delivery pressure. Clear written and spoken communication in English. Nice to Have Working knowledge of Scrapy and other Python-based scraping frameworks. Experience with test automation frameworks. Interest in data science concepts as they apply to data analysis and validation. Interest in using AI and LLM tools to speed up data validation. As a new Zytan, you will: Become part of a self-motivated, progressive, multi-cultural team. Have the freedom and flexibility to work from where you do your best work. Work with cutting-edge open source technologies and tools. 35 days paid holidays

jobs.title: Manual QA Engineer
jobs.description: We are FundCount , an international fintech company with a 20-year track record of delivering innovative solutions. Our unified software platform powers investment, general, and partnership accounting, providing operational efficiency and insights to family offices, fund administrators, and alternative fund managers worldwide. We’re looking for a Manual QA Engineer to join our growing Quality Assurance team. As part of our team, you’ll play a crucial role in ensuring the quality and reliability of our product. You'll engage in manual testing to uncover bugs and work closely with our development team to ensure flawless releases. We are a fully remote company, and you can work from anywhere except Russia and Belarus. About the Product & Team: Our technology stack includes: Java (Hibernate, Spring, Swing, JUnit4, Mockito) Gradle PostgreSQL, MySQL Git We follow a one-month release cycle, freezing code two weeks before each release. We document our processes in Confluence and manage our tasks in Jira (in English). The development team primarily communicates in Russian via Slack. Our QA team consists of 8 engineers. What you will do: Perform thorough manual testing of desktop and web applications. Write detailed bug reports in Jira. Create and maintain test cases in TestRail. Collaborate with developers and product teams throughout the development lifecycle. What we expect from you: 2+ years of experience in manual testing. Solid understanding of Agile methodologies, SDLC, and CI/CD practices. Intermediate or higher English proficiency (written). Ability to independently research and gather information from documentation and public sources. Adaptability to work with different technologies and tools, with a focus-solving rather than specific experience. Technical Skills: Experience testing both desktop and web (frontend and backend) applications. Proficient in SQL and the ability to write DML queries. Confident in working with Windows/Linux terminals.Experience with version control systems (Git). Ability to read and interpret application logs and troubleshoot stack traces. Familiarity with scripting languages like PowerShell, Bash, or cmd/bat. Would be nice if: Basic programming knowledge in any language. Experience or interest in accounting, finance, or investment (e.g., personal involvement in stock markets). We will be glad to offer you: Fully remote work with a flexible schedule. Corporate benefits. Transparent processes with minimal bureaucracy. If you’re ready to contribute to a fast-growing fintech company and work with a talented team, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today! Originally posted on Himalayas

why_matches: Meets the 2+ years of experience requirement (candidate has ~3.5 years of total technical/QA/PM experience).
Has strong hands-on manual QA background, having independently designed and executed QA (test cases, regression cycles, bug triage) at Composity and Ethiojobs.
Possesses the required SQL skills and database concepts for querying and troubleshooting.
Comfortable with Git version control, Jira issue tracking, and working closely with engineering and product teams.
gaps: The job requires testing desktop applications built with Java (Swing, Hibernate, Spring), whereas the candidate's background is primarily in web applications (React, Laravel, PHP, MySQL, ERP/eCommerce/EHR SaaS).
The posting mentions that the development team primarily communicates in Russian via Slack, which could present a communication friction point depending on team integration.
Lacks specific experience with TestRail and Windows/Linux terminal/scripting languages (PowerShell, Bash, cmd/bat) explicitly highlighted in the tech stack requirements.
jobs.reasoning_summary: The candidate brings strong manual QA, SQL, and Agile delivery experience that maps well to the core requirements of the role. However, gaps in specific tech stack elements (desktop/Java apps, TestRail, terminal scripting) and the noted Russian-language communication preference for the dev team introduce some friction, resulting in a moderate match score.

jobs.title: Program Manager, EPD Operations
jobs.description: Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic! About Tailscale Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. Write product requirements. Turn ideas into clear, well-scoped PRDs that give design and engineering what they need to build with confidence. Manage delivery. Organize the work in Jira and keep design, engineering, and QA aligned and moving from kickoff through release. Track what matters. Define and follow the metrics that show how XPN is working for publishers and creators, and use them to guide what we build next. Keep everyone connected. Be the hub for product communication. Share project status, research, and customer insights with the product team. Keep Business Development, Customer Success, and Marketing up to date on what’s shipping and what it means for our partners. Requirements: Product experience. 3+ years in product management or product ownership, shipping software alongside a dedicated engineering team. Customer insight. You enjoy talking with customers and turning those conversations into insights that shape product decisions. You’re comfortable serving more than one type of user and finding solutions that work for everyone involved. Clear writing. You write product requirements that are easy to follow and help the team get aligned quickly. Engineering partnership. You work closely with engineers day to day, making scope and sequencing decisions together, and you’re comfortable managing the backlog and tracking work

jobs.title: Product Manager at Tratta
jobs.description: About Tratta Tratta is the platform that powers credit and collections at scale, and we try to make it enjoyable to work on. Our clients are collection agencies and law firms recovering debt from consumers. Their account data lands in Tratta and is mapped and validated on the way in. They run email and SMS campaigns off it. Consumers land on a payment portal carrying the client's brand, where they can pay, negotiate a plan or sign an agreement electronically without ever speaking to a collector. Payments clear through us by card, ACH or check, and it all feeds back into reporting that shapes the next campaign. Campaigns, data and payments as one closed loop instead of four vendors stitched together. Every week that loop moves millions of dollars in payments, ingests nearly 100 million rows of client data and serves almost 10 million API requests. About the Product Team The product team is small: two PMs, one designer and a distributed engineering team of about ten. You would be our second product hire. There is no product ops layer, no analyst and no one sitting between you and the client, or between you and the code. The role You will own a set of topics end to end. Not "manage a backlog" in the abstract, but pick up messy input from clients and customer success, turn it into something the team can build, get it shipped, and then make sure it actually gets used. Turn requests into work. Client and CS requests arrive as symptoms, not specs. You dig into what is actually being asked, decide whether it is a bug, a gap, a training problem or a real product need, and write it up so a developer can pick it up without a meeting. Prioritize. You decide what gets built next among a lot of competing, legitimate asks, and you can explain the reasoning to a client, a developer and a founder in three different ways. Firefight. Bugs and urgent client issues will land on you. You triage, reproduce, escalate the real ones, and close the loop with whoever raised it. Discovery. You help figure out what we should build next, from client conversations, usage data and your own read of the market. Data. You are comfortable with data end to end: getting it, questioning it, and deciding what to do about it. Own outcomes, not output. Shipping is the midpoint, not the finish line. If a feature launches and nobody knows it exists or nobody adopts it, that is your problem to solve. You will write the client email, record the walkthrough, check the numbers a month later and tell us honestly whether it worked. Wear multiple hats. Small changes you can do yourself with Claude, you do yourself. Otherwise: specs, debugging, data and dashboards, release notes, client emails, whatever the topic needs. There is no one to hand it to. What this role is not It is not a role where you write requirements and hand them to someone else. It is not a role with a defined scope that stays defined. And it is not a role where you can be effective while waiting to be told what to do. How we work Very little process and very few meetings. No planning ritual that exists to justify the previous planning ritual. If something is not working, we change it the next day. The tradeoff is that nothing will be handed to you. There is no queue of pre-groomed tickets, no one checking whether you did the thing, and no process to hide behind if a topic quietly stalls. Autonomy and accountability come as a pair here. We use Claude heavily across product work: analysis, drafting, prototyping, bulk operations across Linear, Slack, HubSpot and our data. Being fluent with AI tooling is not a bonus point, it is how the job gets done at this team size.
